zones.name: Zone I · Construction & Cosmic Design
zones.summary: Hephaestus’s forge, five folds, triple rim, Earth, Sky, Sea, Sun, Moon, Pleiades, Hyades, Orion, and the unbathing Bear.

zones.name: Zone II · The Two Cities: Peace and Law
zones.summary: Torchlit bridal processions, whirling dancers, flutes & lyres; the Agora blood-price dispute, Sacred Circle of Elders, and Two Talents of Gold.

zones.name: Zone III · The Two Cities: War and Ambush
zones.summary: Besieged walls guarded by wives, children, and elders; tall golden Ares & Athena; the river watering-place ambush; Eris, Kydoimos, and crimson Ker.

zones.name: Zone IV · The Labors of the Field
zones.summary: Thrice-ploughed fallow turning black behind the plough; the Silent King’s harvest & oak sacrifice; golden vineyard with kyanos trench, tin fence, and Linus song.

zones.name: Zone V · Cattle, Lions, and Sheep
zones.summary: Lofty-horned oxen of gold and tin by the murmuring river; four golden herdsmen & nine dogs barking and darting back from two terrible lions; white sheep glen.

zones.name: Zone VI · The Dance and the Ocean Rim
zones.summary: Daedalean dancing floor of Knossos for Ariadne, whirling like a potter’s wheel and in rows with two tumblers; the mighty River Oceanus enclosing the shield.

cards.name: The Shield of Achilles — Full 5-Fold Concentric Worldtext (Iliad 18.478–608)
cards.greek: Πρῶτα μὲν σάκος ποίει μέγα τε στιβαρόν τε πάντοσε δαιδάλλων... ἐν δ᾽ ἐτίθει ποταμοῖο μέγα σθένος Ὠκεανοῖο ἄντυγα πὰρ πυμάτην σάκεος πύκα ποιητοῖο.
cards.buckley: First of all he formed a shield, both large and solid, adorning it all over; and around it he threw a shining border, triple, glittering; and from it suspended a silver belt. Five were the folds of the shield itself... And in it he placed the vast strength of the river Oceanus, around the extreme border of the well-formed shield.

worldModel.vision: 84×84 stud concentric 5-fold LEGO disk uniting all five Homeric metals (Gold 297, Silver 179, Bronze 28/84, Tin 71, Kyanos 272/33) from the Cosmic Omphalos to the Oceanus Rim.
worldModel.memory: Simultaneous multi-ring state machine: polar rotation of the Bear, legal turn-taking in the Sacred Circle, river ambush escalation, golden glebe turning black behind the plough, dogs oscillating before the lions, and the Daedalean wheel/row dance.
worldModel.controller: Operative Worldtext (Bolter & Hartsoe): the viewer/warrior navigates from macro-cosmos to micro-scene, probing the rules, memory, and consequences of mortal life.

cards.name: Zone I · Scene 1: Hephaestus’s Forge & The Five-Fold Shield
cards.greek: Πρῶταคลὲν σάκος ποίει μέγα τε στιβαρόν τε πάντοσε δαιδάλλων, περὶ δ᾽ ἄντυγα βάλλε φαεινὴν τρίπλακα μαρμαρέην, ἐκ δ᾽ ἀργύρεον τελαμῶνα.
cards.buckley: First of all he formed a shield, both large and solid, adorning it all over; and around it he threw a shining border, triple, glittering; and from it suspended a silver belt. Five were the folds of the shield itself; but on it he formed many ornaments with cunning skill.

worldModel.vision: Crucible glow of bronze (28), tin (71), gold (297), and silver (179) ingots against basalt forge walls (72); twenty golden-wheeled tripods.
worldModel.memory: Twenty bellows blow into the crucibles by degree as Hephaestus’s work requires; five metallic folds laminate into a single world-surface.
worldModel.controller: Hephaestus hammers the five folds on the great anvil while silver-footed Thetis receives the operative world-shield.

cards.name: Zone I · Scene 2: The Cosmic Boss — Earth, Sky, Sea & The Unbathing Bear
cards.greek: Ἐν μὲν γαῖαν ἔτευξ᾽, ἐν δ᾽ οὐρανόν, ἐν δὲ θάλασσαν, Ἠέλιόν τ᾽ ἀκάμαντα Σελήνην τε πλήθουσαν, ἐν δὲ τὰ τείρεα πάντα, τά τ᾽ οὐρανὸς ἐστεφάνωται, Πληϊάδας θ᾽ Ὑάδας τε τό τε σθένος Ὠρίωνος Ἄρκτον θ᾽, ἣν καὶ Ἄμαξαν ἐπίκλησιν καλέουσιν, ἥ τ᾽ αὐτοῦ στρέφεται καί τ᾽ Ὠρίωνα δοκεύει, οἴη δ᾽ ἄμμορός ἐστι λοετρῶν Ὠκεανοῖο.
cards.buckley: On it he wrought the earth, and the heaven, and the sea, the unwearied sun, and the full moon; on it also, all the constellations with which the heaven is crowned, the Pleiades, the Hyades, and the might of Orion, and the Bear, which they also call by the appellation of the Wain, which there revolves, and watches Orion; but it alone is without a share of the baths of the ocean.

worldModel.vision: Central golden omphalos dome surrounded by kyanos sky (272), emerald earth (2), golden Sun (297/46), silver full Moon (179), and star-stud constellations (11609).
worldModel.memory: Invariance law: The Bear/Wain (Ἄρκτος) revolves perpetually around the polar axis watching Orion, constrained never to dip below the horizon of Oceanus.
worldModel.controller: Cosmological clockwork anchoring all mortal time and agricultural seasons in the outer rings.

cards.name: Zone II · Scene 1: City at Peace — Torchlit Bridal Procession
cards.zoneTitle: The Two Cities: Peace and Law (491–508)
cards.greek: Ἐν δὲ δύω ποίησε πόλεις μερόπων ἀνθρώπων καλάς. ἐν τῇ μέν ῥα γάμοι τ᾽ ἔσαν εἰλαπίναι τε, νύμφας δ᾽ ἐκ θαλάμων δαΐδων ὕπο λαμπομενάων ἠγίνεον ἀνὰ ἄστυ, πολὺς δ᾽ ὑμέναιος ὀρώρει· κοῦροι δ᾽ ὀρχηστῆρες ἐδίνεον, ἐν δ᾽ ἄρα τοῖσιν αὐλοὶ φόρμιγγές τε βοὴν ἔχον· αἱ δὲ γυναῖκες ἱστάμεναι θαύμαζον ἐπὶ προθύροισιν ἑκάστη.
cards.buckley: On it also he fashioned two beautiful cities of articulate-speaking men. In the one, indeed, were marriages and feasts; and they were conducting the brides from their chambers through the city with brilliant torches, and many a bridal song was raised. The young men were dancing in a circle, and among them flutes and lyres gave forth their sounds; and the women standing, each at her portals, admired.

worldModel.vision: White marble colonnades and golden-linteled portals illuminated by trans-orange torches (3959), festive white/gold/lilac chitons, and golden lyres.
worldModel.memory: Processional state transition: brides advance from domestic chambers (θάλαμοι) through public avenues as youths whirl in circular dance.
worldModel.controller: Civic kinship and celebration: acoustic synchronization of hymenaeus song, aulos flute, and phorminx lyre.

cards.name: Zone II · Scene 2: City at Peace — The Sacred Circle & Blood-Price Trial
cards.zoneTitle: The Two Cities: Peace and Law (491–508)
cards.greek: λαοὶ δ᾽ εἰν ἀγορῇ ἔσαν ἀθρόοι· ἔνθα δὲ νεῖκος ὠρώρει, δύο δ᾽ ἄνδρες ἐνείκεον εἵνεκα ποινῆς ἀνδρὸς ἀποφθιμένου... οἱ δὲ γέροντες εἵατ᾽ ἐπὶ ξεστοῖσι λίθοισ᾽ ἱερῷ ἐνὶ κύκλῳ, σκῆπτρα δὲ κηρύκων ἐν χέρσ᾽ ἔχον ἠεροφώνων· τοῖσιν ἔπειτ᾽ ἤϊσσον, ἀμοιβηδὶς δὲ δίκαζον. κεῖτο δ᾽ ἄρ᾽ ἐν μέσσοισι δύω χρυσοῖο τάλαντα, τῷ δόμεν ὃς μετὰ τοῖσι δίκην ἰθύντατα εἴποι.
cards.buckley: But the people were assembled in the forum, for there a strife had arisen, and two men strove for the ransom-money of a slain man; the one affirmed that he had paid all, appealing to the people, but the other denied that he had received any thing; and both wished to find a termination before a judge. The people shouted to both, supporters on either side; and the heralds reined in the people; but the elders sat upon polished stones in a sacred circle, and held in their hands the staves of the loud-shouting heralds; with these then they arose, and adjudged in turn. But there lay in the midst two talents of gold, to give to him who should pronounce a judgment the most correctly.

worldModel.vision: Eight polished white stone seats arranged in a sacred circle around a kyanos pavement; two gleaming talents of gold on the central altar.
worldModel.memory: Procedural legal algorithm: blood-vendetta is converted into deliberative speech; elders rise in turn (ἀμοιβηδὶς) holding the herald’s sceptre; the two talents reward the straightest judgment (δίκην ἰθύντατα).
worldModel.controller: The polis replaces private vengeance with public arbitration.

cards.name: Zone III · Scene 1: City at War — The Besieged Wall & Tall Golden Gods
cards.zoneTitle: The Two Cities: War and Ambush (509–540)
cards.greek: Τὴν δ᾽ ἑτέρην πόλιν ἀμφὶ δύω στρατοὶ εἵατο λαῶν τεύχεσι λαμπόμενοι, δίχα δέ σφισιν ἥνδανε βουλή, ἠὲ διαπραθέειν ἢ ἄνδιχα πάντα δάσασθαι... ἦρχε δ᾽ ἄρα σφιν Ἄρης καὶ Παλλὰς Ἀθήνη ἄμφω χρυσείω, χρύσεια δὲ εἵματα ἕσθην, καλὼ καὶ μεγάλω σὺν τεύχεσιν, ὥς τε θεώ περ, ἀμφὶς ἀριζήλω· λαοὶ δ᾽ ὑπ᾽ ὀλίζονες ἦσαν.
cards.buckley: But around the other city sat two armies of people, glittering in arms; and a plan was agreeable to them, either to destroy it entirely, or to divide all the wealth into two parts, which the pleasant city contained within it. But they did not yet obey, but were secretly arming for an ambush; their beloved wives and young children stood upon the wall guarding it, and together with them the men whom old age possessed. But they advanced; and Mars and Pallas Minerva led them, both golden, and clad in golden garments, beautiful and large with their arms, like gods, both very conspicuous; but the people were smaller.

worldModel.vision: Hieratic scale contrast encoded in LDraw geometry: Ares and Pallas Athena are 11-brick-tall golden colossi while mortal warriors and rampart defenders are 4-brick minifigures.
worldModel.memory: Binary strategic fork (sack vs. divide wealth in half) rejected by the besieged, triggering the covert ambush transition.
worldModel.controller: Divine war-marshals propelling the mortal sortie out from the Scaean ramparts.

cards.name: Zone III · Scene 2: City at War — The River Ambush & Crimson Ker
cards.zoneTitle: The Two Cities: War and Ambush (509–540)
cards.greek: οἱ δ᾽ ὅτε δή ῥ᾽ ἵκανον ὅθι σφίσιν εἶκε λοχῆσαι, ἐν ποταμῷ, ὅθι τ᾽ ἀρδμὸς ἔην πάντεσσι βοτοῖσιν, ἔνθ᾽ ἄρα τοί γ᾽ ἵζοντ᾽ εἰλυμένοι αἴθοπι χαλκῷ... ἐν δ᾽ Ἔρις ἐν δὲ Κυδοιμὸς ὁμίλεον, ἐν δ᾽ ὀλοὴ Κήρ, ἄλλον ζωὸν ἔχουσα νεούτατον, ἄλλον ἄουτον, ἄλλον τεθνηῶτα κατὰ μόθον ἕλκε ποδοῖϊν· εἷμα δ᾽ ἔχ᾽ ἀμφ᾽ ὤμοισι δαφοινεὸν αἵματι φωτῶν.
cards.buckley: But when they now had reached a place where it appeared fit to lay an ambush, by a river, where was a watering-place for all cattle, there they settled, wrapped in shining brass... Then, having formed a line, they fought a battle on the banks of the river, and wounded one another with their brazen spears. Among them mingled Strife and Tumult, and destructive Fate, holding one freshly-wounded, and another unwounded, and by the feet she dragged another, dead, through the affray; and the garment around her shoulders was crimsoned with the blood of men.

worldModel.vision: Kyanos river watering-place (272/33), bronze scouts in olive reeds, white sheep, charging horses, and Ker in dark-red crimson cloak (320).
worldModel.memory: Causal chain: scouts spot herds → ambushers slaughter flocks & piping shepherds → besiegers hear tumult and gallop up → river battle with Eris, Kydoimos, and Ker.
worldModel.controller: Acoustic deception (syrinx pipes vs. battle tumult) and mortal vulnerability.

cards.name: Zone IV · Scene 1: Labors of the Field — The Thrice-Ploughed Fallow
cards.greek: Ἐν δ᾽ ἐτίθει νειὸν μαλακὴν, πίειραν ἄρουραν, εὐρεῖαν τρίπολον· πολλοὶ δ᾽ ἀροτῆρες ἐν αὐτῇ ζεύγεα δινεύοντες ἐλάστρεον ἔνθα καὶ ἔνθα... ἡ δὲ μελαίνετο ὄπισθεν, ἀρηρομένῃ δὲ ἐῴκει χρυσείη περ ἐοῦσα· τὸ δὴ περὶ θαῦμα τέτυκτο.
cards.buckley: On it he also placed a soft fallow field, rich glebe, wide, thrice-ploughed; and in it many ploughmen drove hither and thither, turning round their teams. But when, returning, they reached the end of the field, then a man, advancing, gave into their hands a cup of very sweet wine; but they turned themselves in series, eager to reach the other end of the deep fallow. But it grew black behind, and was like unto ploughed land, though being golden; which was a very great marvel.

worldModel.vision: Golden field plates (297) progressively flipping to black (0) and dark-brown (308) furrowed tiles behind the bronze ploughshare.
worldModel.memory: Iterative loop with state mutation: drive furrow → reach headland → receive cup of sweet wine (δέπας μελιηδέος οἴνου) → turn team → golden metal turns black behind (μελαίνετο).
worldModel.controller: Homer’s supreme neurosymbolic marvel (περὶ θαῦμα τέτυκτο): material gold executing the optical state-change of dark earth.

cards.name: Zone IV · Scene 2: Labors of the Field — The Silent King’s Harvest & Oak Feast
cards.greek: Ἐν δ᾽ ἐτίθει τέμενος βαθύληϊον· ἔνθα δ᾽ ἔριθοι ἤμων ὀξείας δρεπάνας ἐν χερσὶν ἔχοντες... βασιλεὺς δ᾽ ἐν τοῖσι σιωπῇ σκῆπτρον ἔχων ἑστήκει ἐπ᾽ ὄγμου γηθόσυνος κῆρ. κήρυκες δ᾽ ἀπάνευθε ὑπὸ δρυῒ δαῖτα πένοντο, βοῦν δ᾽ ἱερεύσαντες μέγαν ἄμφεπον· αἱ δὲ γυναῖκες δεῖπνον ἐρίθοισιν λεύκ᾽ ἄλφιτα πολλὰ πάλυνον.
cards.buckley: There he also placed a field of deep corn, where reapers were reaping, having sharp sickles in their hands. Some handfuls fell thick in series upon the ground along the furrow, and others the binders of sheaves were tying with straw ropes. Three binders followed the reapers, but behind them boys gathering the handfuls, and carrying them in their arms, continually supplied them; and among them the king in silence, over a furrow, was standing at the staff, rejoicing in his heart. But heralds apart, beneath an oak, were preparing a feast, and having sacrificed a huge ox, they were ministering; and women were strewing much white barley meal as a dinner for the reapers.

worldModel.vision: Golden standing grain stalks, silver sickles (37341d), bound sheaves, the purple-and-gold King with his sceptre, and the spreading oak with white barley meal tiles.
worldModel.memory: Assembly-line pipeline: reapers cut → handfuls fall → boys gather armfuls → three binders tie sheaves → heralds & women prepare the sacrificial ox and barley feast.
worldModel.controller: Ordered reciprocity under the silent, rejoicing gaze of the Basileus.

cards.name: Zone IV · Scene 3: Labors of the Field — The Golden Vineyard & Linus Song
cards.greek: Ἐν δ᾽ ἐτίθει σταφυλῇσι μέγα βρίθουσαν ἀλωὴν καλὴν χρυσείην· μέλανες δ᾽ ἀνὰ βότρυες ἦσαν, ἑστήκει δὲ κάμαξι διαμπερὲς ἀργυρέῃσιν. ἀμφὶ δὲ κυανέην κάπετον, περὶ δ᾽ ἕρκος ἔλασσε κασσιτέροιο· μία δ᾽ οἴη ἀταρπὸς ἐπ᾽ αὐτὴν... τοῖσιν δ᾽ ἐν μέσσοισι πάϊς φόρμιγγι λιγείῃ ἱμερόεν κιθάριζε, λίνον δ᾽ ὑπὸ καλὸν ἄειδε λεπταλέῃ φωνῇ· τοὶ δὲ ῥήσσοντες ἁμαρτῇ μολπῇ τ᾽ ἰυγμῷ τε ποσὶ σκαίροντες ἕποντο.
cards.buckley: On it also he placed a vineyard heavily laden with grapes, beautiful, golden; but the clusters throughout were black; and it was supported throughout by silver poles. Around it he drew a dark-blue trench, and around a hedge of tin; and there was but one path to it, by which the gatherers went, when they collected the vintage. Young virgins and youths, of tender minds, carried the sweet fruit in woven baskets. In the midst of them a boy played pleasantly on a shrill lyre, and sung the beautiful Linus song with a slender voice; while they, beating the ground in accompaniment, with singing and shouting, followed, hopping with their feet.

worldModel.vision: Five-metal polyphony in a single zone: golden vines (297), black clusters (0/22), silver poles (179), dark-blue kyanos trench (272/33), and tin fence (71) with a single path.
worldModel.memory: Topological constraint (μία δ᾽ οἴη ἀταρπὸς — one single path in and out) channeling the rhythmic procession of basket-bearers.
worldModel.controller: The boy’s shrill phorminx and slender Linus song synchronizing the stamping feet of the youths and maidens.

cards.name: Zone V · Scene 1: Pastoral — Oxen of Gold & Tin and the Two Terrible Lions
cards.greek: Ἐν δ᾽ ἀγέλην ποίησε βοῶν ὀρθοκραιράων· αἱ δὲ βόες χρυσοῖο τετεύχατο κασσιτέρου τε... σμερδαλέω δὲ λέοντε δύ᾽ ἐν πρώτῃσι βόεσσιν ταῦρον ἐρύγμηλον ἐχέτην· ὁ δὲ μακρὰ μεμυκὼς ἕλκετο· τὸν δὲ κύνες μετεκίαθον ἠδ᾽ αἰζηοί... ἵσταντο δὲ μάλ᾽ ἐγγύς, ὑλάοντές τε καὶ ἐκτὸς ἀλυσκάζοντες.
cards.buckley: On it he also fashioned a herd of lofty-horned oxen; but the oxen were made of gold and tin; and lowing, they rushed from the stall to the pasture, beside a murmuring river, along the waving reed. Four golden herdsmen accompanied the oxen, and nine dogs, swift of foot, followed them. But two terrible lions among the foremost oxen seized a bellowing bull, and he, dragging, roared loudly; but the dogs and the young men ran up to him. The lions indeed, having torn the hide of the huge ox, were devouring the entrails and the black blood; but the shepherds vainly pressed upon them, urging on the fleet dogs; for they refused to bite the lions, but stood very near, barking, and flying them.

worldModel.vision: Gold (297) and tin (71) horned oxen beside a kyanos river and olive reeds; four golden herdsmen; nine hounds; two tawny lions tearing the bull.
worldModel.memory: Repulsion/attraction boundary dynamics: the four herdsmen urge the nine dogs forward, but the dogs stop short of biting, oscillating between lunging to bark (ὑλάοντες) and darting back (ἀλυσκάζοντες).
worldModel.controller: Wild nature erupting inside pastoral order — the limit of human and canine control.

cards.name: Zone VI · Scene 1: The Daedalean Choros Dance & The River Oceanus Rim
cards.zoneTitle: The Dance and the Ocean Rim (590–608)
cards.greek: Ἐν δὲ χορὸν ποίκιλλε περικλυτὸς Ἀμφιγυήεις, τῷ ἴκελον οἷόν ποτ᾽ ἐνὶ Κνωσῷ εὐρείῃ Δαίδαλος ἤσκησεν καλλιπλοκάμῳ Ἀριάδνῃ. ἔνθα μὲν ἠΐθεοι καὶ παρθένοι ἀλφεσίβοιαι ὠρχεῦντ᾽, ἀλλήλων ἐπὶ καρπῷ χεῖρας ἔχοντες... ὡς ὅτε τις τροχὸν ἄρμενον ἐν παλάμῃσιν ἑζόμενος κεραμεὺς πειρήσεται, αἴ κε θέῃσιν· ἄλλοτε δ᾽ αὖ θρέξασκον ἐπὶ στίχας ἀλλήλοισι... ἐν δ᾽ ἐτίθει ποταμοῖο μέγα σθένος Ὠκεανοῖο ἄντυγα πὰρ πυμάτην σάκεος πύκα ποιητοῖο.
cards.buckley: On it also the illustrious Vulcan embellished a dance, like unto that which in wide Gnossus Daedalus once composed for fair-haired Ariadne. There the youths and the alluring virgins danced, having their hands on each other’s wrists... At one time they would move very lightly with skilled feet, as when a potter sitting shall make trial of a wheel fitted to his hands, whether it will run; and at another time they would move in series towards each other. A large crowd stood around the enjoyable dance, delighted; and among them two tumblers, beginning their song, spun round in the midst. But in it he placed the vast strength of the river Oceanus, around the extreme border of the well-formed shield.

worldModel.vision: Labyrinthine Knossian mosaic pavement in white, gold, and kyanos; maidens in garlands and youths with golden daggers on silver belts; two central tumblers; and the outer ring of River Oceanus.
worldModel.memory: Bimodal choreographic state machine: Mode A = circular rotation like a potter’s trial wheel (τροχός); Mode B = linear counter-marching rows (ἐπὶ στίχας); bounded externally by the continuous circular current of Oceanus.
worldModel.controller: Artifice mirroring artifice: Daedalus’s Knossian choros and the potter’s wheel inside Hephaestus’s shield, closed by the cosmic river.
